```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/midwest_airbnb_extended.db")

listings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
availability = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "availability_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
reviews = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "reviews_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()

DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

# Check the number of rows in each table
nrow(listings)
nrow(availability)
nrow(reviews)
```

## Task 1
```{r}
# Count listings for each host across all three cities
host_counts = listings |>
  dplyr::count(host_id)

# A1: Count hosts with 10 or more listings
host_counts |>
  dplyr::filter(n >= 10) |>
  dplyr::count()

# Attach each host's listing count to their listings
listings_with_hosts = listings |>
  dplyr::left_join(host_counts, by = "host_id")

# A2: Percent of Chicago listings held by hosts with 10+ listings
listings_with_hosts |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Chicago") |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    percent = round(100 * sum(n >= 10) / dplyr::n(), 1)
  )

# B2: Percent of listings held by hosts with 10+ listings in each city
host_shares = listings_with_hosts |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    host_share = 100 * sum(n >= 10) / dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

host_shares |>
  dplyr::mutate(host_share = round(host_share, 1))
```

## Task 2
```{r}
family_value = listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    accommodates >= 4,
    number_of_reviews >= 10,
    review_scores_rating >= 4.8
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    price_per_person = price / accommodates
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, neighbourhood) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    listing_count = dplyr::n(),
    median_price_per_person = median(price_per_person, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(listing_count >= 20)

# A3: Show Columbus neighbourhoods from cheapest to most expensive
family_value |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus") |>
  dplyr::arrange(median_price_per_person)
```

## Task 3
```{r}
city_room_medians = listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, room_type) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    dplyr::across(
      c(price, reviews_per_month, estimated_revenue_l365d),
      ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# A4: Display only the requested revenue value
city_room_medians |>
  dplyr::filter(
    city == "Twin Cities",
    room_type == "Entire home/apt"
  ) |>
  dplyr::pull(estimated_revenue_l365d)
```

## Task 4
```{r}
revenue_shares = listings |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(estimated_revenue_l365d), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    top_10_percent = dplyr::row_number() <= ceiling(0.10 * dplyr::n())
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    percent = 100 *
      sum(estimated_revenue_l365d[top_10_percent], na.rm = TRUE) /
      sum(estimated_revenue_l365d, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# A5: Columbus's percentage, rounded to one decimal
revenue_shares |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus") |>
  dplyr::mutate(percent = round(percent, 1))

# B2: Percent of estimated revenue earned by the top 10% in each city
revenue_shares |>
  dplyr::mutate(percent = round(percent, 1))
```

## Task 5
```{r}
october_shares = availability |>
  dplyr::filter(month == "2026-10") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    listings |>
      dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt"),
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    mostly_taken = nights_available < 0.5 * nights_in_month
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    percent = 100 * sum(mostly_taken) / dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(percent)

october_shares |>
  dplyr::mutate(percent = round(percent, 1))
```

## Task 6
```{r}
monthly_reviews = reviews |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    listings |> dplyr::select(id, city),
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    month >= "2025-07",
    month <= "2026-06"
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, month) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    total_reviews = sum(reviews, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# A8: Twin Cities months, busiest first
twin_cities_reviews = monthly_reviews |>
  dplyr::filter(city == "Twin Cities") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total_reviews))

twin_cities_reviews

# A9: Busiest month's reviews divided by quietest month's reviews
twin_cities_reviews |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    ratio = round(max(total_reviews) / min(total_reviews), 2)
  )
```

## Task 7
```{r}
superhost_medians = listings |>
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    host_is_superhost %in% c("t", "f")
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(city, host_is_superhost) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    median_price = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rating = median(review_scores_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

superhost_medians

# Premium = superhost median price minus other-host median price
superhost_premiums = superhost_medians |>
  dplyr::group_by(city) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    premium = median_price[host_is_superhost == "t"] -
      median_price[host_is_superhost == "f"],
    .groups = "drop"
  )

superhost_premiums
```


## Task 8
```{r}
# Find listings with no matching ID anywhere in availability
missing_availability = listings |>
  dplyr::anti_join(availability, by = "id")

# A10: Count those listings
missing_availability |>
  dplyr::count()

# For the README: Which city loses the most listings?
missing_availability |>
  dplyr::count(city, sort = TRUE)
```
